3. Routing rule: pick the tier for a task. Send to a cheaper tier only when (cheap ceiling + P(cheap fails) x top cost) < top cost AND confidence is high enough; otherwise go straight to a stronger tier. The cheap ceiling defaults to 20% of the estimated top-tier cost for that task. Respect the budget remaining: never start a task whose ceiling does not fit. Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

git push -q -u origin ao/neatlogs-hack-5/routing 2>&1 | tail -3; gh pr create --base main --head ao/neatlogs-hack-5/routing --title "CFO agent: ports, sizer, price history and the routing rule" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

First piece of lane B (`agent/` only).

- `agent/ports.ts`: the interfaces the CFO agent needs from outside: sizing signals, price history, budget remaining, live usage, stop a session, handoff summary, LLM, tracing. Lane A implements them; `agent/testing/fakes.ts` has in-memory versions for tests and dry runs.
- `agent/sizer.ts`: files touched, dependents, tests present and the issue text become small / medium / large plus a confidence score. Rules are deterministic. An optional LLM call (through the port) can raise confidence when it agrees; when it disagrees the larger size wins and confidence drops, so the LLM alone can never make a task cheaper.
- `agent/history.ts`: pass rate and average cost per (size, tier), updated after every attempt, with a prior worth two attempts so the first run works with no data. `PriceHistory.snapshot()` is plain JSON for the engine to save.
- `agent/router.ts`: a cheaper tier is chosen only when `ceiling + P(fails) x top cost < top cost` and confidence is high enough; otherwise a stronger tier. Nothing starts unless its ceiling fits the budget left. Every decision carries a one-sentence reason. Tiers, prices and ceilings come from `tally.yaml`; no model or repo names in code.

## Depends on

Built on #1 (schema and scaffold). Until #1 merges this diff also shows its commits; the lane B changes are everything under `agent/`.

## Tests

`npm test` (58 agent tests pass) and `npm run typecheck`. Covered: cheap chosen when confident, strong chosen when unsure, the break-even maths, learning from repeated failures, nothing started when the budget is too small, ceiling never above budget left, tiers by any name and count, history or signals port failing.

## Known limits and follow-ups

- Prior pass rates and sizing thresholds are guesses until the experiment gives real numbers.
- Watcher, escalation, baseline mode and tracing follow in the next PRs.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2
